newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tax panel's Archer hopes for gains tax cut.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tax panel's Archer hopes for gains tax cut.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, said Friday he will push next year for agreement with the White House on a cut in the capital gains tax rate.

Speaking to reporters, Archer said he still favors complete replacement of the current income tax system with a tax on spending, but acknowledged this was unlikely to occur given the strong opposition from within the Republican party.
He said the committee will also examine which tax credits could be ended, such as the ethanol tax credit, which he called "an anachronism."
"Clearly we are going to be doing taxes. We eagerly await the president's proposals," Archer said at a news conference.

President Clinton's proposals are expected to include a child credit, tuition tax credit and deduction for profits on home sales. But Archer said Republicans will oppose paying for these tax cuts with increased taxes on other groups of taxpayers. To avoid increasing the budget deficit tax cuts must be paid for by reduced spending, he said.

On the issue of capital gains, Republicans are considering a change in House rules which would allow estimates of the loss of revenue to show whether investment and savings increase once the tax is reduced.

The Ways and Means Committee, which also has control over many entitlement programs, will look at short term changes in the Medicare health program for the nation's elderly while a commission studies the need for long-term changes to keep the program solvent.
